newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso launches campaign for May 11 election.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso launches campaign for May 11 election.

text.p: Burkina Faso has launched the campaign for a May 11 parliamentary election, the second since the land-locked West African nation's return to multi-party politics in the 1990s.

The head of the national electoral commission Moussa Sanogo told a news conference launching the campaign on Saturday that 569 candidates representing 13 political parties would contest the 111 seats in the new national assembly.
More than four million people are eligible to vote, 38 percent more than in the first parliamentary election of the transition in 1992.
Sanogo also said that Ghana would lend 7,000 transparent ballot boxes and French experts would supervise provision of indelible ink.
Supporters of President Blaise Compaore in the ruling Congress for Popular Democracy control the outgoing 107-seat assembly.
Compaore came to power after a 1987 coup in which populist leader Captain Thomas Sankara was killed.
Compaore was the sole candidate in the December 1991 presidential election, a poll boycotted by the opposition and in which almost three quarters of voters abstained.
Parliament amended the constitution in January allowing him to stand for a second term in 1998.
